baslik: The Earthquake That Cracked 'Earthquake-Proof' Steel Joints
sonuc: fractured welded steel connections across Los Angeles
tetik: strong shaking on welded beam-column joints
mekanizma: brittle fracture of welded steel moment-frame connections thought to be ductile
ders: steel moment connections were redesigned after the SAC research programme
yanilgi: Most of these steel buildings didn't collapse. The shock was finding cracked joints hidden inside them.
tartisma: The damage was invisible from outside. How many buildings carry hidden cracks after a quake?
basliklar: What the Northridge Earthquake Did to Steel Buildings
The Welds That Were Supposed to Bend
soru: How many cracks are still hidden?
sahneler: An earthquake struck the San Fernando Valley before dawn.
Freeways collapsed and buildings failed, and fifty seven people died.
Then engineers found something alarming.
Welded steel frames had cracked at their joints.
Those joints were supposed to bend without breaking.
Instead, the welds fractured in a brittle way.
The cracks were hidden behind walls and ceilings.
Steel connections were redesigned after a major research programme.

baslik: Why Mid-Rise Buildings Fell in Mexico City
sonuc: collapsed hundreds of buildings far from the epicentre
tetik: shaking amplified by the soft clay of an old lakebed
mekanizma: site amplification and resonance between lakebed soil and mid-rise buildings
ders: Mexico City rewrote its building code for lakebed soils
yanilgi: The epicentre was far away on the coast. The city's soft ground magnified the shaking.
tartisma: Short and very tall buildings often survived while mid-rise ones failed. Should codes depend on the ground beneath?
basliklar: Why Mexico City's Buildings Collapsed in 1985
The Lakebed That Amplified an Earthquake
soru: Should codes depend on the soil?
sahneler: An earthquake off Mexico's Pacific coast shook Mexico City.
Hundreds of buildings collapsed, and thousands of people were killed.
The epicentre was far from the city.
But Mexico City stands on the soft clay of an old lake.
That clay amplified the shaking.
Its rhythm matched mid-rise buildings, and they resonated.
Many short and very tall buildings survived.
Mexico City rewrote its building code for lakebed soils.

baslik: The Brand-New Hospital an Earthquake Tore Apart
sonuc: was wrecked by an earthquake weeks after opening
tetik: a flexible ground storey under a stiff building
mekanizma: soft-storey failure of columns under a much stiffer upper structure
ders: California passed a law requiring hospitals to stay operational after earthquakes
yanilgi: The hospital had just been built to code. The code didn't yet prevent its weak ground storey.
tartisma: A hospital must work after a disaster. Should hospitals meet a higher standard than homes?
basliklar: Why the Olive View Hospital Failed
The New Hospital an Earthquake Wrecked
sahneler: An earthquake wrecked a brand-new hospital near Los Angeles.
Its stair towers collapsed, and ground-floor columns were crushed.
The hospital had opened only weeks earlier.
Its upper floors were stiff and heavy.
The ground floor was flexible and weak.
All the movement concentrated there.
The building had to be demolished.
California then required hospitals to stay operational after earthquakes.

baslik: The Night the Sea Broke Through the Dutch Dikes
sonuc: broke through dikes and flooded the Netherlands
tetik: a storm surge on top of a spring tide
mekanizma: overtopping and breaching of weakened dikes by a storm surge
ders: the Netherlands built the Delta Works
yanilgi: The dikes weren't all swept away by force. Water flowing over the top eroded them from the landward side.
tartisma: Plans to strengthen the dikes existed before the flood. What makes a country finally act?
basliklar: Why the 1953 North Sea Flood Broke the Dikes
The Storm That Created the Delta Works
sahneler: On a winter night, the North Sea broke through the Dutch dikes.
Water rushed into low-lying villages, and one thousand eight hundred thirty six people died.
A storm surge arrived on top of a spring tide.
Water poured over the dikes.
It eroded them from the land side until they breached.
Many people were asleep when the water came.
Plans to raise the dikes already existed.
The Netherlands then built the Delta Works.

baslik: The Town Buried by a Volcano Everyone Had Mapped
tetik: an eruption melting the volcano's ice cap
mekanizma: lahars from melted glacier ice racing down river valleys to the town
ders: volcano monitoring and lahar warning systems were expanded in Colombia
zincir: HAZARD MAP SHOWS ARMERO AT RISK
yanilgi: The disaster was predicted. A hazard map showed Armero was directly in the lahars' path.
tartisma: Residents were told to stay calm hours before the lahars arrived. What makes a warning believable?
basliklar: Why the Armero Tragedy Happened
The Warning That Came Too Late
hook: The danger was on the map
sahneler: At night, volcanic mudflows buried the Colombian town of Armero.
More than twenty three thousand people were killed.
The volcano had shown signs of unrest for months.
A hazard map showed Armero in the danger zone.
The eruption melted part of the ice cap on the summit.
Mudflows raced down river valleys toward the town.
Residents had been told to stay calm.
Colombia expanded volcano monitoring and lahar warnings.

baslik: The City Destroyed in Minutes by a Glowing Cloud
sonuc: was destroyed by a pyroclastic flow
tetik: an eruption sending a superheated cloud down the mountain
mekanizma: a pyroclastic density current reaching the city in minutes
ders: the eruption made pyroclastic flows a central focus of volcano science
yanilgi: Lava wasn't the killer. A fast, superheated cloud of gas and ash swept the city.
tartisma: An election was coming, and officials downplayed the danger. How do politics shape evacuations?
basliklar: Why Saint-Pierre Was Destroyed
The Glowing Cloud That Erased a City
How Mount Pelée Killed a City in Minutes
sahneler: Mount Pelée erupted above the city of Saint-Pierre in Martinique.
Within minutes, a glowing cloud destroyed the city and killed almost everyone.
It wasn't lava.
It was a pyroclastic flow of superheated gas and ash.
The volcano had rumbled for weeks.
Officials downplayed the danger ahead of an election.
Residents stayed.
The eruption made pyroclastic flows central to volcano science.

baslik: A Mountain Fell on a Mining Town
sonuc: buried part of the mining town of Frank
tetik: the collapse of Turtle Mountain's unstable face
mekanizma: rockslide on a naturally unstable slope, likely worsened by coal mining at its base
ders: Turtle Mountain is now continuously monitored
yanilgi: The mine didn't simply dig the mountain down. The slope was unstable already; mining likely helped tip it.
tartisma: The mine reopened within weeks. How quickly should industry return after a disaster?
basliklar: Why the Frank Slide Happened
The Mountain That Fell on a Mining Town
sahneler: Before dawn, part of Turtle Mountain collapsed onto the town of Frank.
In about one hundred seconds, the rock buried homes and killed dozens.
The mountain's face was naturally unstable.
A coal mine was working at its base.
Water and frost had widened cracks in the rock.
The whole mass broke free at once.
The mine reopened within weeks.
Turtle Mountain is now continuously monitored.

baslik: A Hillside Known to Slide Buried a Neighbourhood
sonuc: buried a rural neighbourhood in Washington State
tetik: weeks of heavy rain on an unstable slope
mekanizma: failure of a saturated glacial sediment slope with a long history of landslides
yanilgi: The slope had slid many times before. Earlier reports had warned of a large failure.
tartisma: Homes were permitted below a known landslide area. Who decides where people can build?
basliklar: Why the Oso Landslide Happened
The Slope That Had Slid Before
sahneler: A hillside in Washington State suddenly collapsed.
Mud and debris buried a neighbourhood, and forty three people were killed.
The slope had a long history of landslides.
Earlier reports warned of a larger failure.
Homes had been built in its path.
Weeks of heavy rain saturated the ground.
The slope failed far more violently than expected.
Washington then expanded its landslide mapping.

baslik: The Lake That Released a Cloud of Carbon Dioxide
sonuc: released a deadly cloud of carbon dioxide
tetik: a sudden overturn of gas-saturated deep water
mekanizma: limnic eruption of carbon dioxide dissolved in the lake's deep layers
ders: degassing pipes now vent the lake's carbon dioxide gradually
yanilgi: Nothing exploded or burned. The gas simply flowed downhill and displaced the air.
tartisma: A similar event struck another lake two years earlier. How should science share early warnings?
basliklar: Why Lake Nyos Released a Deadly Gas Cloud
The Lake That Suffocated Its Valleys
sahneler: At night, a lake in Cameroon released a huge cloud of carbon dioxide.
The gas flowed into villages, and one thousand seven hundred forty six people died.
Nothing exploded or burned.
Carbon dioxide from volcanic sources had dissolved deep in the lake.
Something upset the layers, and the gas burst out.
Heavier than air, it flowed down the valleys.
People suffocated where they slept.
Pipes now vent the lake's gas slowly.

baslik: The Elevated Expressway That Toppled Onto Its Side
sonuc: toppled over during the Kobe earthquake
mekanizma: shear and flexural failure of single reinforced concrete piers with inadequate confinement
ders: Japan retrofitted bridge piers and revised seismic design standards
yanilgi: The expressway didn't sink. Its piers failed, and a long section tipped over sideways.
tartisma: Japan had some of the world's strictest codes. What does an earthquake reveal about old standards?
basliklar: Why the Hanshin Expressway Toppled
The Piers That Failed in the Kobe Earthquake
sahneler: The Kobe earthquake struck before dawn.
A long section of elevated expressway toppled onto its side, and thousands died across the region.
The expressway stood on single concrete columns.
They had too little steel wrapping to hold the concrete together.
Under strong shaking, the columns cracked and failed.
The deck tipped over as one piece.
The standards were decades old.
Japan then retrofitted piers and revised its seismic design rules.

baslik: The Neighbourhood That Slid Into the Sea
sonuc: broke up and slid toward the sea
tetik: a great earthquake shaking a layer of sensitive clay
mekanizma: loss of strength in sensitive clay and sand layers, causing a massive landslide
ders: the quake reshaped understanding of subduction zones and ground failure
yanilgi: The houses weren't shaken apart. The ground beneath them flowed and slid.
tartisma: The land later became a park instead of homes. Should unstable land ever be rebuilt?
basliklar: Why Turnagain Heights Slid Into the Sea
The Clay Layer That Gave Way in the 1964 Earthquake
sahneler: A magnitude nine point two earthquake struck Alaska.
For minutes, a whole neighbourhood in Anchorage broke apart and slid toward the sea.
The homes sat on a bluff above a layer of clay.
The long shaking made that clay lose its strength.
The bluff split into blocks that tilted and slid.
Houses were carried hundreds of feet.
The area later became a park.
The earthquake reshaped how engineers study ground failure.

baslik: Tyres Whose Treads Peeled Off at Highway Speed
tetik: tread separation at high speed and heat
mekanizma: separation of the tread and belt from the tyre casing, worsened by low pressure and heat
ders: the US passed the TREAD Act requiring defect reporting and tyre pressure monitors
yanilgi: It wasn't just the tyre or just the vehicle. The interaction between tyre, pressure and SUV mattered.
tartisma: Ford and Firestone blamed each other. When two products fail together, who is responsible?
basliklar: Why Firestone Tyres Shed Their Treads
The Tyre Failures Behind the TREAD Act
sahneler: At highway speed, tyres on Ford Explorers began shedding their treads.
Suddenly the SUVs lost control, and many rolled over.
The tread separated from the tyre's body.
Heat, speed and low pressure made it worse.
Ford and Firestone blamed each other.
Millions of tyres were recalled.
Congress passed the TREAD Act.
New vehicles gained tyre pressure monitors.

baslik: A High-Speed Train Entered a Tight Curve at Over Twice the Limit
tetik: the driver distracted by a phone call from the train staff
mekanizma: overspeed on a curve where automatic speed protection was not in force
ders: Spain added automatic speed protection to more high-speed transitions
yanilgi: The line had advanced train protection, but it ended before this curve.
tartisma: The system relied on the driver at the most demanding point. Where should automation hand over to humans?
basliklar: Why the Santiago de Compostela Train Derailed
The Curve Where Protection Ended
sahneler: A high-speed train derailed on a curve outside Santiago de Compostela.
Carriages were thrown off the track, and dozens of people were killed.
The train entered the curve at more than twice the limit.
The driver was on a work phone call.
Advanced train protection covered the high-speed line.
But it ended before this curve.
Only the driver's braking could slow the train.
Spain then added speed protection to more of these transitions.
